summary.tldr: Changes Canada’s export permit rules for military goods, removes country exemptions, and adds reporting and treaty compliance requirements.
what_it_does: Expands the definition of “arms, ammunition, implements or munitions of war” to include parts, components and technology needed to assemble or use them.
Removes country-based exemptions from the Export Control List for military goods.
Bars the Minister from issuing general export permits and general brokering permits for military goods.

Requires the Minister to consider added factors when deciding export or brokering permits, and to require an end-use certificate when that would help reduce a substantial risk of war crimes or human rights violations.
Requires the Minister to table an annual report in Parliament on military goods exports, permit decisions and steps taken to comply with the Arms Trade Treaty.
Makes permits issued before royal assent expire after 180 days, and gives pending applications and General Export Permit No. 47 temporary transitional treatment.
summary.background: The bill amends the Export and Import Permits Act. Its summary says it is meant to align the law more fully with the Arms Trade Treaty.
